clue.text: Way to rise in the church described by Compton Mackenzie

definitions.text: Way to rise in the church

explanation.surface: A path to clerical promotion as a novelist once portrayed it.
explanation.definitionFit: Steps before an altar lead a cleric upward in a church, and The Altar Steps is a 1922 novel by Compton Mackenzie about a young man entering the priesthood.

clue.text: Those under socialism were discussed by J. B. Priestley

definitions.text: Those under socialism were discussed by J. B. Priestley

parts.words: Those under socialism were discussed by J. B. Priestley
parts.note: points to Priestley's 1947 lecture-pamphlet whose title asks what becomes of painting, music and theatre in a socialist state

explanation.surface: A novelist's essay on the people living under a socialist regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those' looks like people under socialism, but it stands for the cultural pursuits in the title of J. B. Priestley's essay The Arts Under Socialism.
explanation.definitionFit: Priestley's title names painting, music and drama collectively as these creative pursuits.

clue.text: Model heard around Belgium is renowned poet

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car, so 'Model' gives T

indicators.note: the word heard is placed around the Belgian letter, wrapping it

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A fashion model overheard near Belgium turns out to be a famous poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' looks like a homophone signal but is used as written: B goes inside HEARD to make HEBARD, after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare is known by the epithet of the pre-eminent poet of Avon.

clue.text: New fan from China for piano virtuoso

indicators.note: something new is freshly made, so these words are remade into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new fan imported from China is offered to a concert pianist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder: FAN, FROM and CHINA together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Rachmaninoff was a celebrated Russian pianist and composer.

clue.text: Eternal preoccupation of romantic novelist

parts.note: the phrase 'eternal' completes the stock name for a love affair among three people, a staple plot of romance

explanation.surface: What a writer of love stories never stops thinking about.
explanation.definitionFit: The eternal triangle is the familiar love story of two rivals for one partner, endlessly used by romance writers.

clue.text: Article in humorous magazine describes outstanding feature of Falstaff

indicators.note: the article is set within the magazine's name, so 'in' signals insertion

parts.note: Punch was the long-running British satirical weekly
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece in a comic magazine describes what stands out about Shakespeare's fat knight.
explanation.walkthrough: PUNCH was a famous British humour magazine. 'outstanding' is literal: Falstaff's belly sticks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Falstaff is famously fat, and a big protruding belly is his most prominent physical trait.

clue.text: The rest of him is found in Millin's work

definitions.text: The rest of him is found in Millin's work

parts.words: The rest of him is found in Millin's work
parts.note: Sarah Gertrude Millin's 1922 novel bears a title naming the first man's 'rest', so 'him' is that biblical figure

explanation.surface: A missing body is said to turn up in a South African writer's book.
explanation.walkthrough: Millin's novel is Adam's Rest; 'the rest of him' reads as leftover remains but means his place of rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The first man of Genesis is the 'him' whose rest gives the title of Millin's novel.

clue.text: Although he saw his country as tragic he felt it was worth saving

definitions.text: Although he saw his country as tragic he felt it was worth saving

parts.words: Although he saw his country as tragic he felt it was worth saving
parts.note: alludes to two book titles by one American novelist: An American Tragedy and America Is Worth Saving

explanation.surface: A patriot's paradox: a writer who despaired of his nation yet wanted it rescued.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore Dreiser wrote the novel An American Tragedy (1925) and the polemic America Is Worth Saving (1941).

clue.text: Despond anatomized by Democritus Junior

definitions.meaning: despond is an old noun for dejection or low spirits
Robert Burton wrote The Anatomy of ... under the pen name Democritus Junior

explanation.surface: Gloom dissected by a classical philosopher's namesake.
explanation.definitionFit: Despond means low spirits, the gloom that Robert Burton, writing as Democritus Junior, dissected in his 1621 Anatomy.

clue.text: The poet could be thus erotic

indicators.note: says the letters of these words could be arranged as something else

explanation.surface: A suggestion that some poet might write in a sensual vein.
explanation.definitionFit: Theocritus was the Greek poet who founded pastoral verse.

clue.text: Iris Murdoch's sank without a trace

definitions.text: Iris Murdoch's sank without a trace

parts.words: Iris Murdoch's sank without a trace
parts.note: Murdoch's 1958 novel centres on an abbey's medieval chime that once fell into the lake and vanished

explanation.surface: A novelist's book that flopped completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sank without a trace' sounds like a commercial flop; in the novel the old abbey bell lies lost in the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Murdoch's novel The Bell turns on a legendary abbey bell that sank in the lake.

clue.text: I'll run away until I'm bigger, but then I'll fight " said this noble Roman lad

definitions.text: I'll run away until I'm bigger, but then I'll fight " said this noble Roman lad

parts.words: I'll run away until I'm bigger, but then I'll fight " said this noble Roman lad
parts.note: quotes the boy in Coriolanus who speaks these defiant words in Act V when his family pleads with his father

explanation.surface: A Roman boy's boast that he will flee now and fight when grown.
explanation.definitionFit: Young Marcius is the son of Coriolanus in Shakespeare's play and speaks this line.

clue.text: Wesley's way of addressing the colonies

definitions.text: Wesley's way of addressing the colonies

parts.words: Wesley's way of addressing the colonies
parts.note: points to John Wesley's 1775 pamphlet urging the American colonists to stay loyal, titled for its tranquil manner

explanation.surface: How the Methodist preacher spoke to the American colonists.
explanation.walkthrough: John Wesley's tract was A Calm Address to Our American Colonies; 'way' is the manner of the address.
explanation.definitionFit: Wesley's pamphlet described its own manner as untroubled and composed.

clue.text: Norman Lake Poet

parts.note: names a twentieth-century Cumbrian poet with the first name Norman, from the Lake District

explanation.surface: A Norman who belongs among the Lake Poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norman' looks like a Norman Conquest reference, but it is the first name of Norman Nicholson, poet of Millom in the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Nicholson was a poet who lived his whole life in Cumberland, home of the Lake Poets.

clue.text: St Helens players cover a critic

parts.note: St Helens rugby league club are nicknamed the Saints
to bury something is to cover it over

explanation.surface: Rugby players from a Lancashire town shield a reviewer.
explanation.walkthrough: St Helens is a town in northern England whose rugby league team is known as the Saints.
explanation.definitionFit: George Saintsbury was a prolific English literary historian and reviewer.

clue.text: Playwright to liven year's beginnings eagerly

parts.note: John Arden was an English dramatist

indicators.note: the first letters of the three words that follow are taken

explanation.surface: A dramatist sets out to enliven the start of the year with enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with fervour and keenness is doing it zealously.

clue.text: To! the greats —' ancient reign restored" (Pope, The Dunciad)

definitions.text: To! the greats —' ancient reign restored" (Pope, The Dunciad)

parts.words: To! the greats —' ancient reign restored" (Pope, The Dunciad)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Pope's mock epic, where the gap names the ruler of Chaos whose rule returns

explanation.surface: A quotation from Pope with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The line in The Dunciad reads 'Lo! the great Anarch's ancient reign restor'd'; the printed text is a newspaper misreading of 'Lo!' and 'Anarch's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope's word for the ruler of Chaos is a lord of disorder, a bringer of lawlessness.

clue.text: Vicar in proper bloomer

parts.note: prim means primly proper
a rose is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A clergyman wearing prim undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests the underwear, bloomers; it is a flower. Dr Primrose is the hero of Goldsmith's The Vicar of Wakefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Primrose is the clergyman of Goldsmith's novel The Vicar of Wakefield.

clue.text: Council condemning iconoclasts in Midi town quarter

parts.note: Nice is a city in the south of France, the Midi
NE, northeast, is a compass quarter

explanation.surface: A church council meets in a district of a southern French town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Second Council of Nicaea (787) condemned iconoclasm, the destruction of religious images.
explanation.definitionFit: The councils held at Nicaea, including the one of 787 that restored icons, take this adjective.

clue.text: Daily improved condition of Shakespeare after Bowdler?

definitions.meaning: a daily is a British term for a domestic help who comes in to clean

definitions.text: improved condition of Shakespeare after Bowdler?
definitions.meaning: Thomas Bowdler issued a family Shakespeare with the rude bits removed, leaving the text purer

explanation.surface: A newspaper on how Shakespeare looked after the censor had finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a charwoman who does housework, and Bowdler's expurgated Shakespeare was more decent, less smutty than before.

clue.text: Protector of Storey's stage work

definitions.meaning: the Lord Protector ruled England in the 1650s
David Storey's 1973 play is named after that ruler

explanation.surface: A guardian of a novelist's theatrical output.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Cromwell held the title Lord Protector, and David Storey wrote a play named after him.

clue.text: High priest is rising on abridgement

parts.note: Eli was the high priest at Shiloh in the Book of Samuel

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is goes upward, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: A senior cleric getting up to speak about a shortened text.
explanation.definitionFit: Elision shortens a word or text by leaving out a sound or passage, a kind of cutting down.

clue.text: Usual peruser of Woolf

definitions.meaning: Virginia Woolf's essay collections are titled for an ordinary reader

explanation.surface: An ordinary reader of a modernist novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Common means ordinary, and Woolf's essay collections are called The Common Reader.

clue.text: It becomes unavailable as soon as booked

definitions.text: It becomes unavailable as soon as booked

parts.words: It becomes unavailable as soon as booked
parts.note: 'booked' reads like a reservation, but here it means filled with books

explanation.surface: Something that sells out the moment a reservation is made, like a hotel room.
explanation.definitionFit: Space on a shelf is used up once volumes are put on it.

clue.text: Egyptian god in Maugham story

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: An Egyptian deity appears in a Somerset Maugham tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset Maugham's short story about a missionary and a prostitute in Samoa is titled after the weather.

clue.text: She agreed to Acton in sibling solidar tity

definitions.text: She agreed to Acton in sibling solidar tity

parts.words: She agreed to Acton in sibling solidar tity
parts.note: refers to the Brontë sister who, like her sisters, took a Bell pen name, hers being Acton

explanation.surface: A woman consents to something for her sisters' sake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acton' looks like a place or the historian; it is the pen name Acton Bell taken by Anne Brontë alongside Currer and Ellis. 'solidar tity' is a newspaper misprint of 'solidarity'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Brontë published as Acton Bell, matching her sisters Charlotte and Emily.

clue.text: Reportedly deserves essential elements of Hydriotaphia

indicators.note: signals that the word for deserves is to be taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to earn something is to deserve it

explanation.surface: Someone is said to merit the core parts of Sir Thomas Browne's treatise.
explanation.walkthrough: Hydriotaphia, or Urn Burial (1658), is Sir Thomas Browne's meditation on burial vessels found in Norfolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Browne's Hydriotaphia is built around funerary vessels unearthed in Norfolk.

clue.text: "1 do desire you not to deny this —" (Merchant of Venice)

definitions.text: "1 do desire you not to deny this —" (Merchant of Venice)

parts.words: "1 do desire you not to deny this —" (Merchant of Venice)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Portia's words to Lorenzo in Act III, asking him to accept a burden she lays on him

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The '1' is a newspaper misreading of 'I'. Portia asks Lorenzo to take charge of her house while she is away.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia's word means a burden or charge laid upon someone.

clue.text: Shaw's enduring archbishop

parts.note: in Back to Methuselah, Shaw has a cleric who lives for centuries and becomes archbishop of a northern English see

explanation.surface: A long-serving church leader from a Shaw play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enduring' means long-lived: in the part The Thing Happens, the Archbishop of York is shown to be nearly 300 years old.
explanation.definitionFit: The archbishop in Shaw's play holds the see of the northern English cathedral city.

clue.text: Hidden meaning needs runes, perhaps

indicators.note: suggests these letters might perhaps be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Interpreting a secret message requires ancient letters, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: An undersense is a subtext, a meaning lying beneath the surface.
